epithet.en: A Moorish general in the service of Venice

2.modern-en: Othello calmly meets Brabantio's accusation of having bewitched Desdemona and is summoned to the Duke about the Turkish threat.

3.modern-en: Othello defends his marriage before the Venetian senate by telling the story of his courtship, and Desdemona herself confirms her choice.

4.modern-en: Othello lands safely in Cyprus, reunites with Desdemona, and is hailed as the saviour of the island.

6.modern-en: Othello breaks up the drunken brawl on the watch and demotes Cassio for losing his discipline.

8.modern-en: Othello receives Iago in the castle while Cassio confers separately with Desdemona about regaining favour.

9.modern-en: Othello is worked on by Iago through the long temptation scene and ends it swearing vengeance on Cassio and Desdemona.

10.modern-en: Othello demands the handkerchief from Desdemona and rages at her when she cannot produce it.

11.modern-en: Othello, half-out of his senses, falls into a trance and then watches Iago stage a duped overhearing of Cassio's talk about Bianca.

12.modern-en: Othello strikes Desdemona in front of the Venetian envoy Lodovico and ushers her out as a whore.

13.modern-en: Othello orders Desdemona to bed and tells her, in cold half-civility, what he intends to do.

14.modern-en: Othello is offstage while Iago orchestrates the attack on Cassio in the street; the noise of it reaches him.

15.modern-en: Othello enters the bedchamber, smothers Desdemona, learns the truth from Emilia, asks to be remembered as he was, and kills himself on the bed.

epithet.en: Othello's ensign and the play's antagonist

1.modern-en: Iago opens the play complaining to Roderigo that Othello has passed him over for Cassio, and stirs Brabantio out of bed with the news of Desdemona's marriage.

2.modern-en: Iago pretends loyalty to Othello and warns him that Brabantio is coming.

3.modern-en: Iago lays out the first version of his plan in a soliloquy: he will hint to Othello that Cassio is too familiar with Desdemona.

4.modern-en: Iago lands in Cyprus, banters with Desdemona on the quay, and confides his next steps to the audience.

5.modern-en: Iago dispatches the herald's announcement of celebration and lays the trap for Cassio's drinking.

6.modern-en: Iago gets Cassio drunk, engineers the brawl that costs him his post, and tells him afterwards to ask Desdemona for help.

7.modern-en: Iago plays the helpful friend to Cassio outside the castle in the early morning.

8.modern-en: Iago waits while Cassio meets with Desdemona and reports the meeting to Othello with a knowing pause.

9.modern-en: Iago carries Othello through the long temptation scene step by step, using his wife Emilia to pass him the dropped handkerchief at the end.

10.modern-en: Iago listens to Othello's furious questioning of Desdemona and is asked, for the first time, how she should be killed.

11.modern-en: Iago stages a conversation with Cassio about Bianca and lets Othello overhear it as proof of the affair.

12.modern-en: Iago receives Lodovico from Venice, lets Othello strike Desdemona publicly, and pretends afterwards to be appalled.

13.modern-en: Iago counsels Roderigo to murder Cassio in the street and lays out the night's plan.

14.modern-en: Iago ambushes Cassio with Roderigo, wounds him from behind, kills Roderigo to silence him, and pretends to investigate the scene.

15.modern-en: Iago is exposed by Emilia in the bedchamber, kills her on the spot, refuses to explain himself, and is led off to be tortured.

epithet.en: Othello's wife, daughter of the senator Brabantio

3.modern-en: Desdemona is summoned to the Senate, confirms that she married Othello of her own will, and asks to follow him to Cyprus.

4.modern-en: Desdemona lands in Cyprus, banters with Iago while she waits for Othello's ship, and is reunited with him.

6.modern-en: Desdemona is briefly woken by the brawl and helped back to bed by Othello.

9.modern-en: Desdemona drops the handkerchief Othello gave her without noticing, then keeps pressing him to take Cassio back.

10.modern-en: Desdemona is interrogated about the handkerchief and refuses to lie even as Othello grows violent.

11.modern-en: Desdemona is summoned by Lodovico and is shocked when Othello strikes her in front of the visiting Venetian.

12.modern-en: Desdemona is called a whore by Othello in private and questioned about Cassio; afterwards she cannot bring herself to repeat the word to Emilia.

13.modern-en: Desdemona sings the Willow Song to Emilia as she prepares for bed, half-aware that something very bad is coming.

15.modern-en: Desdemona wakes to find Othello over her, swears her innocence one last time, and is smothered; her last words exonerate him.

epithet.en: Othello's lieutenant, newly promoted over Iago

2.modern-en: Cassio comes to summon Othello to the Senate about the Turkish threat.

3.modern-en: Cassio is at the Senate as Othello presents his case and is named to convoy Desdemona to Cyprus.

4.modern-en: Cassio arrives first at Cyprus, greets Desdemona with elaborate courtesy, and prepares the castle for Othello's arrival.

6.modern-en: Cassio gets drunk on the watch at Iago's urging, brawls with Montano, and is cashiered by Othello.

7.modern-en: Cassio commissions the morning musicians outside the castle and asks Iago to arrange a meeting with Desdemona.

8.modern-en: Cassio meets Desdemona in private and is promised her help.

9.modern-en: Cassio is seen leaving Desdemona by Othello, providing the first piece of 'evidence' Iago needs.

10.modern-en: Cassio is brought before Desdemona again to press his suit while Othello watches from a distance.

11.modern-en: Cassio chats with Iago about Bianca and is overheard by Othello, who takes the laughter to be about Desdemona.

14.modern-en: Cassio is ambushed in the dark street, wounded in the leg by Iago from behind, and brought into the castle alive.

15.modern-en: Cassio is named the new governor of Cyprus in the closing scene and given the duty of disposing of Othello's estate.

4.modern-en: Emilia arrives in Cyprus with Iago and is greeted, more warmly than her husband expected, by Cassio.

9.modern-en: Emilia picks up the dropped handkerchief and gives it to Iago, knowing he wants it and not knowing why.

10.modern-en: Emilia watches Othello berate Desdemona about the handkerchief and is asked afterwards if she has seen it.

12.modern-en: Emilia is called in by Othello as if she were the keeper of a brothel and asked about Desdemona's conduct.

13.modern-en: Emilia helps Desdemona prepare for bed and listens to the Willow Song, telling her that men are men and worth no more than they are.

15.modern-en: Emilia raises the alarm when she finds Desdemona dead, works out what her husband has done, refuses to be silenced, and is killed by Iago for telling the truth.

epithet.en: A wealthy Venetian gentleman in love with Desdemona

1.modern-en: Roderigo opens the play complaining that Iago has not delivered Desdemona despite the money he has handed over.

2.modern-en: Roderigo is at the street arrest of Othello with Brabantio.

3.modern-en: Roderigo despairs over Desdemona at the end of the Senate scene and is talked by Iago into following her to Cyprus.

5.modern-en: Roderigo is at the herald's announcement of celebration on Cyprus.

6.modern-en: Roderigo is used by Iago to provoke Cassio in the drunken brawl.

10.modern-en: Roderigo complains to Iago that he has spent all his money and seen no return.

14.modern-en: Roderigo attacks Cassio in the dark street and is killed by Iago to keep him quiet about the conspiracy.

1.modern-en: Brabantio is roused from sleep by Iago and Roderigo with the news that Desdemona has eloped with Othello.

2.modern-en: Brabantio confronts Othello in the street with a small armed company and accuses him of bewitching Desdemona.

3.modern-en: Brabantio presents his case to the Senate, hears Desdemona side with Othello, and warns the general she may deceive him as she has deceived her father.

epithet.en: A courtesan in Cyprus, in love with Cassio

10.modern-en: Bianca finds Cassio at the castle gate, accuses him of neglecting her, and is handed the strawberry handkerchief to copy.

11.modern-en: Bianca returns the handkerchief in the street, throwing it back at Cassio in front of the hidden Othello.

14.modern-en: Bianca runs to Cassio after the ambush, weeps over his wound, and is hauled away by Iago as if she were responsible.
